questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of skeletal muscle?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Striated appearance**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Skeletal muscles** are characterized by a distinct **striated appearance** when viewed under a microscope, which is caused by the highly organized arrangement of internal **contractile proteins**.
 
• This striation is due to repeating units called **sarcomeres**, which contain thick filaments made of **myosin** and thin filaments made of **actin**.
 
• The regular overlapping of these filaments creates alternating **dark A-bands** (anisotropic) and **light I-bands** (isotropic), resulting in the visible transverse stripes.
 
• Unlike other muscle tissues, skeletal muscle is under **voluntary control**, meaning its contraction is consciously directed by the **somatic nervous system** to move the **skeletal system**.
 
• Each skeletal muscle cell, or **muscle fiber**, is a **multinucleated syncytium**, where multiple **nuclei** are located at the **periphery** of the cell just beneath the **sarcolemma** (plasma membrane).

• Exhibits a **non-striated appearance** because its **myofilaments** are not arranged into sarcomeres.

• **Cardiac Muscle**:

• Contains specialized cell junctions called **intercalated discs** that allow for synchronized **contractions**.
 
• Cells are generally **branched** and possess **one or two central nuclei**.

questions.question: A concave mirror produces a virtual, erect and magnified image when the object is positioned _________.

options.text: Between the focus and the pole
Between the centre of curvature and the focus

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Between the focus and the pole**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **concave mirror**, also known as a **converging mirror**, is a spherical mirror with a reflecting surface that curves inward toward the **centre of curvature**.
 
• When an object is placed **between the principal focus (F) and the pole (P)**, the distance of the object is less than the **focal length (f)** of the mirror.
 
• Light rays from the object strike the mirror and **diverge** upon reflection; these rays do not meet on the real side of the mirror.
 
• By extending these reflected rays backward, they appear to intersect at a point **behind the mirror**, creating a **virtual image**.
 
• This specific image is **erect** (upright) and **magnified** (larger than the actual object), with a **magnification (m)** value greater than 1.
 
• This unique optical property is why **concave mirrors** are extensively used as **shaving mirrors**, **makeup mirrors**, and by **dentists** to see enlarged views of teeth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Beyond the centre of curvature:**

 
 
• When the object is located beyond **C**, the rays converge to form a **real, inverted, and diminished** image between **C and F**.
 
 
 
• **At the principal focus:**
 
 
• Placing the object exactly at **F** results in reflected rays that are **parallel** to the principal axis, forming a **real, inverted, and highly magnified** image at **infinity**.
 
 
 
• **Between the centre of curvature and the focus:**
 
 
• In this position, the light rays converge to form a **real, inverted, and magnified** image **beyond C**.
 
 
 
• **At the centre of curvature:**
 
 
• When the object is at **C**, the mirror produces a **real and inverted** image that is the **same size** as the object, located exactly at **C**.

questions.question: The magnitude of force on a conductor in a magnetic field increases when ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Current increases**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **magnetic force** acting on a **straight conductor** of length **L** carrying a steady current **I** and placed in a uniform external **magnetic field** **B** is given by the formula **F = B I L sin(θ)**.
 
• In this expression, **F** represents the magnitude of the force, **B** is the **magnetic field strength** (or magnetic flux density), **I** is the **electric current** flowing through the wire, and **θ** is the angle between the direction of the current and the magnetic field.
 
• Since the force **F** is **directly proportional** to the current **I** (**F ∝ I**), any increase in the magnitude of the current leads to a corresponding increase in the **mechanical force** exerted on the conductor.
 
• The relationship also dictates that the force is **maximum** when the conductor is positioned **perpendicular** to the magnetic field lines (where **θ = 90°** and **sin(90°) = 1**).
 
• Conversely, reducing variables such as the **magnetic field strength** or the **active length** of the wire within the field will result in a decrease in the total force magnitude.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fleming's Left-Hand Rule**:

 
 
• This rule is used to determine the **direction of the force**; when the thumb, forefinger, and middle finger of the left hand are held **mutually perpendicular**, the **Thumb** points to the **Force**, the **Forefinger** to the **Magnetic Field**, and the **Middle finger** to the **Current**.
 
 
 
• **Zero Force Condition**:
 
 
• The force experienced by the conductor is **minimum (zero)** if it is placed **parallel** or **anti-parallel** to the magnetic field lines, as **sin(0°)** or **sin(180°)** equals zero.
 
 
 
• **Applications**:
 
 
• This principle is the fundamental basis for the operation of **electric motors**, where electrical energy is converted into **mechanical work** through the interaction of currents and magnetic fields.
 
• It is also applied in **moving coil galvanometers** and **loudspeakers** to translate current variations into physical movement.

questions.question: Plastids, which are found only in plant cells, help in:

• **Leucoplast Types**:

• **Elaioplasts**: Responsible for storing **oils** and **fats** within the plant tissue.

questions.question: Which of the following statements correctly explains the position of sodium (Na) in the activity series of metals?

options.text: Sodium is less reactive than copper and cannot displace it from salt solution.
Sodium does not react with water, hence placed at the bottom of the series.
Sodium is more reactive than hydrogen and displaces it from acid.
Sodium is less reactive than hydrogen and hence placed below it.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sodium is more reactive than hydrogen and displaces it from acid**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Activity Series** (or reactivity series) of metals is a list where metals are arranged in the decreasing order of their chemical reactivity; **Sodium (Na)** is positioned near the top, indicating high reactivity. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• Sodium is far more reactive than **Copper (Cu)**, as it sits much higher in the series. It can easily displace copper from its salt solutions, such as **Copper(II) Sulfate**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• Sodium reacts violently and exothermically with **cold water** to produce **Sodium Hydroxide (NaOH)** and **Hydrogen gas (H₂)**, which often catches fire due to the heat evolved. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• In the activity series, **Hydrogen (H)** is used as a reference point; metals like **Sodium**, **Potassium**, and **Calcium** are placed above hydrogen because they can reduce hydrogen ions from dilute acids. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• When sodium reacts with a dilute acid like **Hydrochloric acid (HCl)**, it undergoes a **single displacement reaction**: 2Na + 2HCl → 2NaCl + H₂. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Reactivity Trends**:

 
 
• The series starts with **Potassium (K)** as the most reactive, followed by **Sodium (Na)**, **Lithium (Li)**, and **Calcium (Ca)**.
 
• Metals at the bottom, such as **Gold (Au)** and **Platinum (Pt)**, are known as **noble metals** because of their lack of reactivity.
 
• Sodium has an **Atomic Number of 11** and belongs to the **Alkali Metals (Group 1)** of the periodic table.
 
• Due to its extreme reactivity with oxygen and moisture, sodium is always stored under **Kerosene** or liquid paraffin to prevent accidental combustion.
 
• Sodium is so soft that it can be easily cut with a **knife**, revealing a shiny metallic surface that tarnishes rapidly in air.

questions.question: An element X has two isotopes: ₆X¹² and ₆X¹⁴. Both are electrically neutral and chemically identical, but one of them is unstable and radioactive. Which of the following statements best explains why ₆X¹⁴ is radioactive, even though both isotopes have the same number of protons and electrons?

options.text: Because ₆X¹⁴ has excess neutrons, causing imbalance in nuclear forces
Because ₆X¹⁴ has equal numbers of protons and neutrons, making it energetically unstable
Because ₆X¹⁴ has more electrons than protons, leading to instability in electron distribution
Because ₆X¹⁴ has a smaller nucleus that cannot hold neutrons tightly, resulting in spontaneous decay

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Because 6X14 has excess neutrons, causing imbalance in nuclear forces**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Isotopes** are variants of a particular chemical element which differ in **neutron number**, although all isotopes of a given element have the same number of **protons** in each atom. In this case, element X has an **atomic number** of 6, identifying it as **Carbon**.
 
• The isotope ₆X¹² contains **6 protons** and **6 neutrons**, resulting in a **neutron-to-proton (n/p) ratio** of 1:1, which is highly stable for light nuclei.
 
• The isotope ₆X¹⁴ contains **6 protons** and **8 neutrons**. This **excess of neutrons** increases the n/p ratio to approximately 1.33:1, moving it away from the **belt of stability**.
 
• **Radioactivity** is a nuclear phenomenon where an **unstable nucleus** undergoes spontaneous transformation to reach a more stable, lower-energy state by emitting radiation.
 
• In ₆X¹⁴, the imbalance between the **short-range strong nuclear force** (which attracts nucleons) and the **long-range electrostatic repulsion** between protons leads to nuclear instability, making the atom **radioactive**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Carbon-14 (₆C¹⁴)**:

 
 
• It is a heavy, radioactive isotope of carbon used primarily in **radiocarbon dating** to determine the age of organic artifacts.
 
• It has a **half-life** of approximately **5,730 years**.
 
• The decay process involves **Beta (β−) emission**, where a neutron is converted into a proton, an electron, and an antineutrino, transforming the atom into stable **Nitrogen-14**.
 
 
 
• **Strong Nuclear Force**:
 
 
• This is the fundamental force that holds protons and neutrons together in the **nucleus**.
 
• It is independent of charge, meaning it acts equally between proton-proton, neutron-neutron, and proton-neutron pairs at very small distances (approx. 1 femtometer).
 
 
 
• **Nuclear Binding Energy**:
 
 
• It is the minimum energy required to disassemble a nucleus into its constituent nucleons.
 
• Unstable isotopes like ₆X¹⁴ have a lower **binding energy per nucleon** compared to their stable counterparts.

questions.question: In the chemical equation xPb(NO₃)₂(s) → yPbO(s) + zNO₂(g) + wO₂(g), what are the values of x, y, z and w?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**x = 2 ; y = 2 ; z = 4 ; w = 1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• This chemical equation represents the **thermal decomposition** of **lead(II) nitrate**, a process where a single solid reactant breaks down into a solid oxide and two distinct gases when **heat energy** is applied.
 
• To balance the equation, we analyze the atoms on the **Left Hand Side (LHS)**: Lead (Pb) = x, Nitrogen (N) = 2x, and Oxygen (O) = 6x.
 
• On the **Right Hand Side (RHS)**, the total atom count is: Lead (Pb) = y, Nitrogen (N) = z, and Oxygen (O) = y + 2z + 2w.
 
• Applying the **Law of Conservation of Mass**, we set the number of atoms of each element equal on both sides: for lead, x = y; for nitrogen, z = 2x.
 
• Substituting these relationships into the oxygen balance equation (6x = y + 2z + 2w) gives 6x = x + 2(2x) + 2w, which simplifies to 6x = 5x + 2w, resulting in the ratio x = 2w.
 
• By assigning the simplest whole numbers, if w = 1, then x = 2, which leads to y = 2 and z = 4. The fully balanced equation is 2Pb(NO₃)₂(s) rightarrow 2PbO(s) + 4NO₂(g) + O₂(g) .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lead(II) Nitrate (Pb(NO₃)₂)**:

 
 
• It is an **inorganic compound** typically appearing as colorless crystals or a white powder.
 
• It serves as a strong **oxidizing agent** and is used in the manufacturing of matches and specialized explosives.
 
 
 
• **Nitrogen Dioxide (NO₂)**:
 
 
• This is a **reddish-brown toxic gas** with a pungent, sharp odor.
 
• In laboratory experiments, the appearance of **brown fumes** during heating is a standard diagnostic observation for the presence of the **nitrate ion**.
 
 
 
• **Lead(II) Oxide (PbO)**:
 
 
• Commonly known as **litharge**, this solid residue appears as a **yellow-colored** substance after the decomposition reaction is complete.
 
• It is **amphoteric** in nature, meaning it possesses the chemical property to react with both acids and bases to form salts and water.

questions.question: Which of the following statement about a solution is correct?

options.text: The solute in a solution settles down on standing.
The solute in a solution is always present in a greater amount than the solvent.
A solution is a heterogeneous mixture of two or more substances.
A solution is a homogeneous mixture in which the solute particles are not visible to the naked eye.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A solution is a homogeneous mixture in which the solute particles are not visible to the naked eye.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **solution** is defined as a **homogeneous mixture** of two or more substances, meaning its composition and properties are uniform throughout the entire sample. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• The particles in a true solution are extremely small, with a diameter less than **1 nanometer (10−⁹ meter)**. Due to this microscopic size, they cannot be seen by the **naked eye** and do not scatter a beam of light. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• In a solution, the **solute particles** do not settle down when left undisturbed for a long period, which indicates that a solution is **chemically stable**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• A solution consists of a **solvent** (the component present in the **larger amount**) and a **solute** (the component present in the **smaller amount**). ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Types of Mixtures**:

 
 
• **Suspension**: This is a **heterogeneous mixture** containing large solute particles (greater than **1000 nm**) that eventually **settle down** under the influence of gravity.
 
• **Colloid**: A mixture where particle size is intermediate (between **1 nm and 1000 nm**). While it may appear homogeneous, it is **heterogeneous** and exhibits the **Tyndall effect**.
 
 
 
• **Physical Characteristics of Solutions**:
 
 
• Solute particles cannot be separated from the mixture by physical **filtration** processes because they pass through the filter paper.
 
• Solutions can exist in any phase of matter, such as **gaseous solutions** (air), **liquid solutions** (lemonade), and **solid solutions** (alloys like **brass**).
 
• The **concentration** of a solution is determined by the mass or volume of solute dissolved in a specific volume of solvent.

questions.question: In some plants, a meristematic tissue is found at the base of leaves or near the nodes, separating regions of a mature tissue. Which tissue is this?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Intercalary meristem**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Intercalary meristems** are a specific type of **meristematic tissue** located at the **base of leaves** or the **internodes** (the regions between two nodes) of plants.
 
• These tissues are essentially remnants of the **apical meristem** that have been separated from the tip by the development of **permanent tissues** during plant growth.
 
• The primary function of this tissue is to promote the **rapid elongation** of stems and leaves, which is particularly evident in **monocotyledons** such as **grasses**, **bamboo**, and **sugarcane**.
 
• A crucial ecological role of **intercalary meristems** is that they allow for the **regeneration** of plant parts that are removed or damaged by **grazing herbivores**.
 
• They are classified as **primary meristems** because they appear early in the life of a plant and contribute significantly to the formation of the **primary plant body**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Apical Meristem**:

 
 
• Located at the **growing tips** of roots and shoots (the **root apex** and **shoot apex**).
 
• Responsible for **primary growth**, which increases the length of the plant along its main axis.
 
 
 
• **Lateral Meristem**:
 
 
• Found on the **lateral sides** of stems and roots, running parallel to the long axis.
 
• Includes tissues like the **vascular cambium** and **cork cambium**, which are responsible for **secondary growth** (increasing the thickness or **girth** of the plant).
 
 
 
• **Differentiated Tissue**:
 
 
• Refers to cells that have undergone **differentiation**, a process where they achieve a specialized structure and **permanent function**.
 
• These cells, such as **parenchyma**, **sclerenchyma**, or **xylem**, typically lose the **power of division** under normal conditions.

questions.question: What is the audible frequency range for human beings?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**20 Hz to 20,000 Hz**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **audible range** of sound for human beings is generally considered to be between **20 Hz** and **20,000 Hz** (or **20 kHz**).
 
• **Frequency** is defined as the number of sound wave cycles per second, and it is measured in the SI unit **Hertz (Hz)**.
 
• The human ear is most sensitive to the frequency range between **2,000 Hz** and **5,000 Hz**, which is the range where most **human speech** occurs.
 
• Sound waves are longitudinal mechanical waves that require a medium to travel; the human ear detects these pressure variations through the **tympanic membrane** and **cochlea**.

• In **Physics**, this type of movement is a form of **oscillatory motion**. When the frequency of these oscillations falls within the range of **20 Hz to 20,000 Hz**, it becomes audible to the human ear as sound.

Mathematically, this is expressed as **F = G(m1 × m2) / r²**, where **F** represents the gravitational force.

• **Medium Independence:**
 
 
• Gravitational force is independent of the **intervening medium**. Whether two masses are kept in **water**, air, or a vacuum, the gravitational force between them remains unchanged as **G** is a universal constant.
 
 
 
• **Universal Gravitational Constant (G):**
 
 
• The value of **G** is approximately **6.674 × 10−¹¹ Nm²/kg²**, which indicates that gravity is a relatively **weak force** unless at least one of the masses involved is planetary in scale.

• Alternatively, the **removal of oxygen** or any other electronegative element from a compound is also classified as **reduction**, as seen in the extraction of metals from their oxides.

__
 
• The term **Formula Unit Mass** is specifically employed for substances whose constituent particles are **ions**. Unlike **covalent compounds** which consist of discrete molecules, **ionic compounds** exist as a continuous three-dimensional **crystal lattice**. ***Hence, statement I is correct.***
 
• The **Formula Unit Mass** is defined as the sum of the **atomic masses** of all atoms present in the **empirical formula** or the **formula unit** of an ionic compound. It represents the mass of the simplest ratio of ions in the substance. ***Hence, statement II is correct.***

questions.question: A student notices that Hydra creates new organisms by developing small protrusions on its body, which eventually detach. What kind of reproduction is this?

__
 
• **Hydra** is a freshwater organism belonging to the phylum **Cnidaria**, known for its remarkable biological processes and **regenerative** abilities.
 
• **Budding** is a specific form of **asexual reproduction** where a new individual originates from a specialized generative anatomical point on the parent organism.
 
• In **Hydra**, the process is initiated by repeated **mitotic cell divisions** at a specific site, leading to the formation of a small **protrusion** or **outgrowth** known as a **bud**.
 
• As the **bud** matures, it develops essential structures such as **tentacles** and a **mouth** while remaining physically attached to the parent, receiving nutrients through the parent's **gastrovascular cavity**.
 
• Upon reaching a certain level of maturity and size, the new **Hydra** constricts at the base, **detaches** from the parent body, and begins life as an **independent**, **genetically identical** clone.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

• In **Hydra**, this typically occurs under unfavorable environmental conditions to ensure **genetic diversity** and survival.
 
 
 
• **Regeneration**:
 
 
• The process of **renewing** or **restoring** lost or damaged tissues, organs, or entire body parts.
 
• While **Hydra** exhibits extreme **morphallaxis** (reorganization of existing tissues), regeneration is generally a **repair mechanism** rather than a primary planned reproductive strategy like budding.
 
 
 
• **Parthenogenesis**:
 
 
• A type of asexual reproduction where an **embryo** develops from an **unfertilized egg** cell.
 
• This phenomenon is observed in various **invertebrates** (like rotifers and bees) and some **vertebrates**, but it is not the mechanism used by **Hydra** for forming body protrusions.

questions.question: Which statement correctly explains the role of decomposers in an ecosystem?

__
 
• **Decomposers**, primarily consisting of **bacteria** and **fungi**, are **heterotrophic organisms** that break down complex organic matter from dead plants and animals into simpler inorganic forms.
 
• They perform the critical function of **nutrient cycling** by releasing essential elements like **Nitrogen**, **Phosphorus**, and **Potassium** back into the soil, which are then reused by **primary producers**.
 
• The process of decomposition involves several stages, including **fragmentation**, **leaching**, **catabolism**, **humification**, and **mineralization**, facilitated by **extracellular enzymes** secreted by these organisms.
 
• By digesting **detritus** (dead organic matter), decomposers act as the **natural scavengers** of the ecosystem, preventing the accumulation of waste and maintaining the **ecological balance**.
 
• They represent the final link in the **Detritus Food Chain (DFC)**, ensuring that the flow of matter in an ecosystem remains **cyclic** rather than linear.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

• They use **chlorophyll** to trap **solar energy** and convert inorganic substances like **carbon dioxide** and water into energy-rich **organic compounds** (glucose). This relates to the incorrect options describing energy production from sunlight.
 
 
 
• **Saprotrophs:**
 
 
• This term specifically refers to decomposers that feed by absorbing nutrients from decaying matter through **osmophagy**.
 
• Unlike **Detritivores** (e.g., earthworms), which ingest and fragment waste internally, saprotrophs break down matter externally.
 
 
 
• **Trophic Levels:**
 
 
• In a **Grazing Food Chain**, energy moves from producers to **herbivores** and then to **carnivores**. Decomposers bridge the gap between all levels by processing the remains of every organism once they die.

questions.question: A device has a resistance of 75 Ω and carries a current of 4 A. The power dissipated is _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1200 W**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Resistance (R)** is defined as the property of a conductor that opposes the flow of electric current. In the given problem, the resistance of the device is specified as **75 Ω**.
 
• **Electric Current (I)** is the rate of flow of electric charge through a cross-section of a conductor. The device carries a steady current of **4 A**.
 
• The **Electric Power (P)** dissipated by a resistive component is the rate at which electrical energy is converted into **heat energy**.
 
• The relationship between power, current, and resistance is given by the formula: **P = I² × R**. This is derived from **Ohm's Law** and the basic power formula **P = V × I**.
 
• To find the power dissipated, we substitute the given values into the formula: **P = (4 A)² × 75 Ω**.
 
• First, calculate the square of the current: **4² = 16**.
 
• Then, multiply the result by the resistance: **16 × 75 = 1200**.
 
• The resulting value for the power dissipated is **1200 Watts (W)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ohm's Law**:

 
 
• States that **V = I × R**, where V is potential difference, I is current, and R is resistance.
 
• By substituting **V/R** for I or **I × R** for V in the power formula, we obtain alternative expressions: **P = V² / R** and **P = V × I**.
 
 
 
• **Unit of Power**:
 
 
• The **SI unit** of power is the **Watt (W)**, named after the Scottish inventor **James Watt**.
 
• One Watt is defined as the consumption of energy at the rate of **one Joule per second** (1 J/s).
 
 
 
• **Joule's Law of Heating**:
 
 
• Describes the heat produced in a resistor as **H = I² × R × t**, where t is the time for which current flows.
 
• This principle is utilized in **electric heaters**, irons, and toasters.

questions.question: The motion of the moon around the earth requires a centripetal force, which is provided by _____________.

options.text: The internal forces of the moon
The force of attraction of the earth

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The force of attraction of the earth**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to **Newton's First Law of Motion**, an object will continue in a straight line unless acted upon by an external force. For the **Moon** to move in a nearly circular orbit around the **Earth**, its direction of motion must constantly change, which requires a **centripetal force** directed toward the center of the circle.
 
• The **gravitational force** of attraction between the **Earth** and the **Moon** provides this necessary **centripetal force**. Without this force, the **Moon** would fly off in a **tangential** straight-line path due to its **inertia**.
 
• This interaction is governed by **Newton's Universal Law of Gravitation**, which states that every particle in the universe attracts every other particle with a force that is directly proportional to the product of their **masses** and inversely proportional to the square of the **distance** between their centers.
 
• The magnitude of the **gravitational force** (F) is calculated using the formula F = G × M × m / r², where **G** is the **Gravitational Constant**, **M** is the mass of the **Earth**, **m** is the mass of the **Moon**, and **r** is the distance between them.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Centripetal Force**:

 
 
• It is not a new kind of force but a role played by existing forces like **gravity**, **tension**, or **friction**.
 
• For an object of mass **m** moving at velocity **v** in a radius **r**, it is expressed as F = mv² / r.
 
 
 
• **Inertia**:
 
 
• **Inertia** is the inherent property of matter by which it resists any change in its state of rest or uniform motion.
 
• In the **Moon's** orbit, **inertia** explains why the **Moon** wants to move forward, while **gravity** pulls it inward, resulting in a curved path.
 
 
 
• **Internal Forces**:
 
 
• These are forces exerted by particles of a system on each other. According to **Newton's Third Law**, they occur in equal and opposite pairs and cannot change the **motion of the center of mass** of the system.

• The **Left Ventricle** is the strongest chamber of the heart, pumping oxygenated blood into the **Systemic Circulation** through the **Aorta** to supply the body's tissues. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• Purification, or the exchange of gases, occurs within the **Lungs**; therefore, the blood sent from the heart to the lungs must be deoxygenated (depleted of oxygen) to be refreshed. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• In the **Pulmonary Circuit**, the **Right Ventricle** contracts to eject deoxygenated blood into the **Pulmonary Artery**, which carries it directly to the **Lungs** for oxygenation. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pulmonary Artery and Veins**:

 
 
• The **Pulmonary Artery** is unique as it is the only artery in the adult human body that carries **Deoxygenated Blood**.
 
• The **Pulmonary Veins** are the only veins that carry **Oxygenated Blood**, transporting it from the lungs to the **Left Atrium**.
 
 
 
• **Heart Valves**:
 
 
• The **Pulmonary Valve** prevents the backflow of blood from the pulmonary artery into the **Right Ventricle**.
 
• The **Tricuspid Valve** regulates blood flow between the **Right Atrium** and the **Right Ventricle**.
 
 
 
• **Gaseous Exchange**:
 
 
• This occurs at the **Alveoli** where **CO₂** diffuses out of the blood and **O₂** diffuses into the **Red Blood Cells** to bind with **Hemoglobin**.
 
 
 
• **Double Circulation**:
 
 
• Humans have a **Four-Chambered Heart** that ensures complete separation of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood, allowing for efficient **Metabolic Activity**.

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of all organic compounds?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**They always contain carbon**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Organic compounds** are a vast class of chemical substances characterized by the presence of **carbon** atoms covalently bonded to other elements. The study of these molecules is the core of **organic chemistry**.
 
• The **tetravalency** of carbon enables it to form **four covalent bonds**, allowing for the creation of stable and complex molecular architectures including **linear chains**, **branched structures**, and **aromatic rings**.
 
• Carbon possesses the unique property of **catenation**, which is the ability of an element to form **long-chain polymers** or rings by bonding with atoms of the same element. This is why millions of organic compounds exist.
 
• While **hydrogen** is present in the vast majority of organic compounds (forming **hydrocarbons**), the presence of **carbon** is the sole universal requirement. Even compounds like **carbon tetrachloride (CCl₄)** are considered organic despite lacking hydrogen.
 
• The distinction between organic and inorganic was historically based on the **Vital Force Theory**, but since **Friedrich Wohler** synthesized **urea** in **1828**, the definition has shifted strictly to the **carbon-centric** chemical composition.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bonding Nature**:

 
 
• Organic compounds predominantly feature **covalent bonds**. **Ionic bonds** are typical of inorganic salts like **Sodium Chloride (NaCl)**, where electrons are transferred rather than shared.
 
 
 
• **Heteroatoms**:
 
 
• **Oxygen** and **Nitrogen** are common in organic functional groups like **alcohols (−OH)**, **carboxylic acids (−COOH)**, and **amines (−NH₂)**.
 
• However, they are not present in **hydrocarbons** such as **Methane (CH₄)**, **Propane (C₃H₈)**, or **Benzene (C₆H₆)**, meaning they are not a universal characteristic of all organic substances.
 
 
 
• **Exceptions**:
 
 
• Simple carbon-containing compounds like **carbonates**, **cyanides**, and **carbon oxides** (e.g., **CO₂**) are traditionally classified as **inorganic** due to their properties and historical context.

questions.question: A body covers a straight-line distance of 10 m from point A to B in 5 s and then covers back the distance from point B to point A along the same straight path in 5 s. How much will be the average speed of the body?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2 m/s**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Average Speed** is defined as the **total distance** traveled by an object divided by the **total time** taken to cover that distance.
 
• In this scenario, the body moves from **point A to point B**, covering a straight-line distance of **10 meters**.
 
• The body then travels back from **point B to point A** along the same path, covering the same distance of **10 meters** again.
 
• The **Total Distance** covered for the entire journey is calculated as: 10 m + 10 m = **20 meters**.
 
• The time taken for the first leg is **5 seconds**, and the time for the return leg is also **5 seconds**. Thus, the **Total Time** taken is: 5 s + 5 s = **10 seconds**.
 
• Applying the formula for speed: **Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time**. Substituting the values gives: 20 m ÷ 10 s = **2 m/s**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Average Velocity vs. Speed**:

 
 
• While **Average Speed** is a **scalar quantity** (only magnitude), **Average Velocity** is a **vector quantity** (magnitude and direction).
 
• Because the body returns to its starting point, the net **displacement** is **0 meters**. Therefore, the **average velocity** for this journey is **0 m/s**.
 
 
 
• **SI Units**:
 
 
• The **International System of Units (SI)**, established in **1960**, identifies **meters per second (m/s)** as the standard unit for speed and velocity.
 
• To convert **m/s** to **km/h**, the value is multiplied by **3.6**; thus, 2 m/s is equivalent to **7.2 km/h**.
 
 
 
• **Uniform Motion**:
 
 
• If an object covers equal distances in equal intervals of time, it is in **uniform motion**. Here, the speed is constant at **2 m/s** for both halves of the trip.

questions.question: Which of the following metals forms an amphoteric oxide when reacting with air?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Aluminium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Amphoteric oxides** are defined as metallic oxides that can react with both **acids** and **bases** to produce **salt** and **water**, thereby demonstrating both acidic and basic characteristics.
 
• When **Aluminium (Al)** is exposed to **air**, it reacts with **oxygen** to form a thin, stable protective layer of **Aluminium Oxide ( Al₂O₃ )** on its surface.
 
• The **basic nature** of Al₂O₃ is demonstrated when it reacts with **Hydrochloric acid (HCl)** to form **Aluminium chloride**: Al₂O₃ + 6HCl rightarrow 2AlCl₃ + 3H₂O .
 
• The **acidic nature** of Al₂O₃ is demonstrated through its reaction with a strong base like **Sodium hydroxide (NaOH)** to form **Sodium aluminate**: Al₂O₃ + 2NaOH rightarrow 2NaAlO₂ + H₂O .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Basic Oxides**:

 
 
• **Sodium (Na)** and **Potassium (K)** are highly reactive **alkali metals** that form **Sodium Oxide ( Na₂O )** and **Potassium Oxide ( K₂O )**, which are strictly basic and react with water to form strong **alkalis**.
 
• **Calcium (Ca)** reacts with oxygen to form **Calcium Oxide (CaO)**, commonly known as **Quicklime**, which is a basic oxide and turns red litmus blue when dissolved in water.
 
 
 
• **Other Amphoteric Examples**:
 
 
• Beyond **Aluminium**, other metals that form amphoteric oxides include **Zinc (ZnO)**, **Lead (PbO)**, and **Tin (SnO)**.
 
• These oxides are crucial in **industrial chemistry**, particularly in the manufacturing of **glass**, **ceramics**, and as **catalysts** in organic synthesis.

questions.question: Which of the following distinguishes the Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum from the Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**RER has ribosomes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER)** is a large, membrane-bound network of sacs and tubules found in **eukaryotic cells**, serving as a primary site for molecular synthesis and transport.
 
• The **Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum (RER)** is physically distinguished by the presence of numerous **ribosomes** attached to its outer membrane surface, which give it a granular or rough appearance under **electron microscopy**.
 
• In contrast, the **Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum (SER)** is characterized by a complete lack of **ribosomes**, resulting in a smooth, tubular structure.
 
• The presence of **ribosomes** on the **RER** facilitates its primary function: the **translation** and **synthesis of proteins**, particularly those intended for secretion or for use in **lysosomes** and the **plasma membrane**.
 
• The **SER** serves distinct roles, primarily focusing on **lipid biosynthesis**, **steroid metabolism**, and the **detoxification** of lipid-soluble drugs and metabolic wastes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum (RER)**:

 
 
• It is often continuous with the **nuclear envelope**, allowing for efficient transport of mRNA.
 
• It contains **chaperone proteins** that assist in the proper **folding** of newly synthesized polypeptide chains.
 
• It is highly developed in cells that specialize in **protein secretion**, such as **pancreatic cells** (secreting insulin) and **plasma cells** (secreting antibodies).
 
 
 
• **Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum (SER)**:
 
 
• It is responsible for the synthesis of **phospholipids** and **cholesterol**, which are critical for **membrane biogenesis**.
 
• In the liver, **SER** enzymes like **Cytochrome P450** are vital for **detoxifying** various chemicals.
 
• In **striated muscle cells**, a specialized form called the **sarcoplasmic reticulum** regulates **calcium ion** concentrations, which is essential for **muscle contraction**.

questions.question: A body moves 6 km towards the east in 1 hour and then 8 km towards the west in the next 1 hour. The average velocity of the body for the whole journey is ___________ .
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1 km/h west**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Average velocity** is defined as the total **displacement** of an object divided by the **total time** taken for the journey. Unlike speed, velocity is a **vector quantity**, meaning it possesses both **magnitude** and **direction**.
 
• To calculate **net displacement**, we must assign a sign convention to the directions. Usually, **East** is taken as positive (+) and **West** is taken as negative (−). Following this, the first displacement is +6 km and the second displacement is −8 km.
 
• The **net displacement** is the algebraic sum of individual displacements: 6 km + (−8 km) = −2 km. The negative sign indicates that the **resultant displacement** is **2 km towards the west** from the starting point.
 
• The **total time** elapsed for the journey is the sum of the individual time intervals, which is 1 hr + 1 hr = 2 hrs.
 
• Applying the formula for **average velocity**:

 Average Velocity = Net Displacement / Total Time

 Average Velocity = −2 km / 2 hrs = −1 km/h.

 The magnitude is **1 km/h** and the direction is **West**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Difference between Average Speed and Average Velocity**:

 
 
• **Average Speed** is a **scalar quantity** calculated by dividing the total **distance** by the total time. In this case, total distance = 6 km + 8 km = 14 km. Thus, **Average Speed** = 14 km / 2 hrs = 7 km/h.
 
• **Average Velocity** can be **zero** or negative depending on the **displacement**, whereas **average speed** is always positive if the body is in motion.
 
 
 
• **Vector Properties**:
 
 
• **Displacement** is the **shortest straight-line distance** between the initial and final positions. If a body returns to its **original position** after any amount of travel, its displacement and consequently its **average velocity** will be zero.

questions.question: Ethanoic acid reacts with sodium carbonate to produce:

options.text: Sodium acetate, carbon dioxide, and water

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sodium acetate, carbon dioxide, and water**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ethanoic acid**, also known as **acetic acid**, is a weak organic acid represented by the chemical formula **CH₃COOH**.
 
• When ethanoic acid reacts with **sodium carbonate** (Na₂CO₃), it undergoes a characteristic **acid-carbonate reaction**, which is a type of neutralization.
 
• The reaction produces three distinct products: a salt called **sodium acetate** (CH₃COONa), **carbon dioxide** (CO₂) gas, and **water** (H₂O).
 
• The balanced chemical equation for this interaction is: **2CH₃COOH + Na₂CO₃ → 2CH₃COONa + H₂O + CO₂**.
 
• This reaction is physically marked by **brisk effervescence** due to the rapid evolution of **carbon dioxide** gas.
 
• The formation of **sodium acetate**, a salt of a weak acid and a strong base, results in a solution that is slightly **alkaline** in nature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ethanoic Acid Properties:**

 
 
• It is the main ingredient of **vinegar**, typically making up **5% to 8%** of the solution by volume.
 
• Pure ethanoic acid is called **glacial acetic acid** because its melting point is **290 K (16.6 °C)**, causing it to freeze during cold climates.
 
• It belongs to the homologous series of **carboxylic acids** and is widely used as a **preservative** in pickles.
 
 
 
• **Sodium Carbonate (Washing Soda):**
 
 
• It is an inorganic compound with the formula **Na₂CO₃** and is often used as a **water softener** in laundry and for manufacturing glass.
 
 
 
• **Carbon Dioxide Testing:**
 
 
• The presence of **CO₂** produced in this reaction can be verified using the **lime water test**. When the gas is passed through lime water (calcium hydroxide), it turns **milky** due to the formation of insoluble **calcium carbonate**.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Sodium Bicarbonate:**
 
 
• Ethanoic acid also reacts with **sodium hydrogen carbonate** (baking soda) to produce the same products: **CH₃COOH + NaHCO₃ → CH₃COONa + H₂O + CO₂**.

questions.question: If 12 J of work is done to move a charge of 2 C between two points, what is the potential difference between these points?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**6 V**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **electric potential difference** between two points in an electric circuit is defined as the amount of **work done** (W) in moving a unit **electric charge** (Q) from one point to the other.
 
• The fundamental mathematical relationship for electric potential is expressed as: **Potential Difference (V) = Work Done (W) / Charge (Q)**.
 
• According to the problem statement, the amount of **work done** to move the charge is **12 Joules (J)**.
 
• The magnitude of the **electric charge** being moved between the two specified points is given as **2 Coulombs (C)**.
 
• By substituting these values into the formula, we calculate the potential difference as: **V = 12 / 2**, which results in a value of **6**.
 
• Since the units of measurement are in the **International System of Units (SI)**, the resulting potential difference is expressed in **Volts (V)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Electric Potential (Volt)**:

 
 
• The **SI unit** of electric potential difference is the **Volt**, named in honor of the Italian physicist **Alessandro Volta**.
 
• One **Volt** is defined as the potential difference between two points when **one Joule** of work is done to move a charge of **one Coulomb** from one point to the other (**1 V = 1 J/C**).
 
• It represents the **electrical pressure** or tension that drives the flow of electrons through a conductor.
 
 
 
• **Measurement and Instrumentation**:
 
 
• The potential difference is measured using a device called a **Voltmeter**.
 
• A **voltmeter** is always connected in **parallel** across the component or points where the potential difference is to be measured.
 
• It possesses a very **high resistance** so that it takes a negligible current from the circuit, ensuring accurate readings.
 
 
 
• **Electric Charge and Energy**:
 
 
• The **Coulomb (C)** is the SI unit of electric charge, equivalent to the charge transported by a constant current of one ampere in one second.
 
• The charge of a single electron is approximately **1.6 × 10−¹⁹** Coulombs, meaning one Coulomb consists of roughly **6.242 × 10¹⁸** electrons.

questions.question: A 90 W electric bulb does how much work in 10 seconds?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**900 J**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Power** is defined as the rate at which **work** is done or **energy** is consumed per unit of **time**.
 
• The fundamental relationship between these physical quantities is given by the formula **Power (P) = Work Done (W) / Time (t)**.
 
• To calculate the total **work done** by the **electric bulb**, the formula is rearranged to **Work (W) = Power (P) × Time (t)**.
 
• The problem provides a **Power rating** of **90 W** and a **Time interval** of **10 seconds**.
 
• Substituting the given values into the equation results in: **Work = 90 W × 10 s = 900 J**.
 
• This calculation confirms that the bulb performs **900 Joules** of work over the specified duration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Units and Definitions**:

 
 
• The **Watt (W)** is the **SI unit of power** and is equal to one **Joule per second (1 J/s)**.
 
• The **Joule (J)** is the **SI unit of energy** and work, representing the energy transferred when a force of one **Newton** acts through a distance of one **meter**.
 
• The **power rating** of an appliance indicates how much **electrical energy** it converts into other forms (like **light** or **heat**) every second.
 
 
 
• **Practical Applications**:
 
 
• In **domestic electricity billing**, energy is often measured in **kilowatt-hours (kWh)** rather than Joules due to the large scale of consumption.
 
• One **kilowatt-hour** is equivalent to **3.6 × 10⁶ Joules**.
 
• Efficiency in **electric bulbs** is measured by how much of the total **work done** is actually converted into **visible light** versus wasted **thermal energy**.
